gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-im-fell-english-sc: IM Fell English SC sets a bookish text serif with soft contrast in every curve, and its a, c, e and s keep open throats. Bruno Ace's wire-like tubes stand opposite it.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-inria-serif: Dignified in manner, Inria Serif has wide-mouthed round letters and diagonals a touch lighter than its verticals. Bruno Ace gives the page its curves without any thinning, drawn like tubing, and that rigid line is the strongest thing here.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-joan: Ruler-straight and expressive up top, then softer below. Bruno Ace has no swelling where curves meet stems, while Joan's bowls shift gently in weight, so paragraphs would feel classic and unhurried.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-junge: Junge reads with authority, its curves leaving generous gaps. Bruno Ace holds every stroke to one width, while Junge's low-to-medium contrast would carry a long page with a dignified, steady pace and a faintly candle-flame taper.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-kameron: Bruno Ace draws a consistently thick outline with no thinning anywhere, and it lingers on each character. Kameron answers with the tempered contrast of a lightly flexed spring wire, and its curves refuse to close.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-libertinus-serif: Bruno Ace is all tubelike, constant-weight line. Libertinus Serif adds a slight swell on its bowls and an open s, so a long passage would read refined and authoritative, with gentle shifts in weight.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-libre-caslon-text: Libre Caslon Text lifts the pen early, leaving its curves unfinished, with low-key thick-thin variation. Bruno Ace has no modulation at all, so give Libre Caslon Text the larger size, since its gradual weight change needs room.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-lustria: Lustria reads traditional and authoritative, its thin parts only slightly slimmer than the stems and its lowercase a wide-mouthed. Bruno Ace's zero stroke contrast makes the strongest foil.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-maitree: Dignified in its restraint, Maitree swells measuredly from hairline to stem, with open-mouthed curves on c, e and s. Bruno Ace excels at round, unvarying outlines; Maitree at quiet thick-and-thin.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-marcellus: Marcellus has a subtle weight change like etched lines in glass, and its rounded letters stay clearly open at the side. Bruno Ace's monoline construction against that faint texture is the strongest quality here.
